Zhujiajiao an ancient water town located in the Qingpu District on the outskirts of Shanghai, China. Often referred to as the "Venice of Shanghai," it is a popular tourist destination known for its well-preserved traditional architecture, canals, and stone bridges. Key Features and Attractions Canals and Bridges: The town is built around a network of canals, with over 36 ancient stone bridges still in use, including the iconic Fangsheng Bridge, a five-arch stone bridge that is a landmark of the town. Ancient History: Established about 1,700 years ago, the town has a rich history, with archaeological findings in the area dating back 5,000 years. Traditional Architecture: Visitors can explore numerous well-preserved Ming and Qing dynasty-era houses and gardens. Boat Rides: Gondola-style boat rides along the canals offer a unique perspective of the town's charming streets and houses. Ke Zhi Yuan (Ke Family Garden): A large, traditional Chinese garden featuring a man-made hill, a pond, and various pavilions, offering a peaceful retreat. North Street (Bei Dajie): The main street is lined with ancient shops, restaurants, and tea houses, providing a vibrant glimpse into local life and commerce. Visiting Zhujiajiao is easily accessible from central Shanghai by bus or metro, making it a popular day-trip destination for those looking to experience the charm of an ancient Chinese water town without traveling far from the modern metropolis.

The Zhujiajiao Ancient Water Town is an important tourist destination, about one hour drive from Shanghai city. The Town was established nearly 1700 years ago, famous for stone bridges, waterways and Ming and Qing dynasty architecture. It's also called The "Venice of Shanghai". Its very enjoyable to spend time there, walking along the waterways, taking a boat cruise or relaxing with a cup of tea. Other places to visit is the landmark Kenzi garden established in 1912. It has a main hall, a garden, and an artificial hill. Fangsheng Bridge is another attraction, best among the 36 ancient stone bridges, It was built in 1812 and supposed to be the largest stone arch bridge in Shanghai. The Zhujiajiao Ancient Water Town is so beautiful that one can easily spend an entire day there, but a minimum of three hours is needed to see it.

If you do not have time to visit Suzhou or Hangzhou, here is a great place to see the ancient town built along the intricate waterways. Shops are mostly the same as what you could find in a typical Chinese ancient town selling more or less the same items, so I would instead spend more time reading up the history behind the town. This is accessible from Shanghai city using Metro line 17. However, the journey could take roughly 1.5hr. So do plan your time and take into consideration the long travel time Visited on 2 January 2025, Thursday. No tickets required, free entry.

Review for Zhujiajiao ancient Water Town. To reach there you can take subway from Shanghai Hongqiao subway station. "Wonderful place! Zhujiajiao Water Town is incredibly well-preserved, with its ancient charm still intact. You'll love strolling along the canals, crossing the many bridges, and taking in the historic architecture. The old houses on the canal banks have been beautifully transformed into restaurants, shops, and local produce stores. A highlight is the ancient post office turned museum, where you can send letters to yourself or loved ones from special post boxes - they'll be mailed to you in a specific month of a future year of your choice! What a unique experience! Perfect for a relaxing day trip or a romantic getaway. Highly recommended!" 5/5 stars

The canal was busy with the occasional boat rides rowing past, the bridges were crowded with people taking photos, especially those who dressed up in the period dresses from the numerous shops offering this service. It was quaint & delightful to observe. A good place to spend half a day or so + lunch in the number of interesting inns there.

A Charming Getaway Just Outside Shanghai Zhujiajiao Ancient Town may not be as large as some other ancient towns, but it’s the perfect size for a slow-paced exploration — with just enough winding alleys, bridges, and a few classic cafes where you can relax and take in the atmosphere. We highly recommend spending at least one night here, and if possible, come on a weekday. We checked in on a Monday and while there were still some tourists, the town was much quieter and more enjoyable without the weekend crowds. Staying overnight really allows you to appreciate the peaceful charm once the day-trippers leave. We stayed at Shiyuan Inn, located right inside the ancient town. After searching through many options, we found that most hotels in the area have been modernized. Shiyuan Inn is one of the rare few that still retains its traditional, classic interior — which added so much character to our stay. Getting here is super convenient from Shanghai, with direct access via metro. If you're looking for a short escape from the city with a touch of old-world charm, this is a great option.

Zhujiajiao Ancient Town, often called the "Venice of Shanghai," is a well-preserved water town with over 1,700 years of history. Located about 50 km from downtown Shanghai, it features picturesque canals, stone bridges, ancient architecture, and traditional tea houses. Key highlights include: - Fangsheng Bridge - Kezhi Garden - North Street - Boat Rides Zhujiajiao is perfect for a day trip from Shanghai, combining history, culture, and local delicacies like Zongzi (sticky rice dumplings) and lotus root dishes. The ancient town is bustling with tourists and offers local food and Chinese costume shops along the walkway. However, the prices inside are slightly higher than elsewhere, but it seems like customers are willing to pay. The atmosphere is pleasant and perfect for photos. It's a good option if you have a free day to explore.

Approx. 1 hour car ride from the Bund area. Zhujiaqiao is old town with lots of food outlets selling dried fruits, preserve veges and chilli and much more. Not a bad way to spend the day away from Shanghai. Highly recommended to visit a Taiwanese cafe, 可成小吃，near the South Gate entrance. Oyster omelette, Taiwanese beef noodles and stinky tofu are few of specials there, owners are Taiwanese and extremely friendly. Another place worth of visiting is the bottle paining art shop, 德藝軒，the artist paints and writes using a hair-thin brush from inside of the bottle create some amazing pictures, truly spectacular! Have a look at the video, the master artist was also very friendly and chatty. Overall, although like many other Chinese tourist sites, very commercially-oriented, but i managed to find at least two lovely places and made few friends there!

Zhujiajiao Ancient Town is a beautiful place with gardens, narrow streets, bridges, boats and many shops. Line 17 brings you to Zhujiajiao Station, it's almost a 40 minute ride from Hongqiao Railway Station. When arriving with the metro, it's still a 30 minute walk to the entrance of the ancient town. There are maps and signs around the town to guide you there. You can also take a bus or even a boat. First of all, I'd recommend to buy the package/combination ticket for 60RMB per person. You'll be able to visit Kezhi Garden, The Garden Of Inseparable Hearts, and Shanghai Helong Art Gallery. It wasn't too crowded when I visited in the winter, but I can't imagine how busy these narrow streets can get in the spring or summer. There are so many places to get a drink or eat some food, so I also recommend staying at Zhujiajiao until it gets dark and the lights start to ignite. The sunset can also be very picturesque, so keep an eye on the time and the place you want to be to get these photos at the perfect time. Yuanjin Temple is a great place to get a nice view of the ancient town of Zhujiajiao, because it allows you to go the first floor and walk around the balcony.

An hour and 15 minutes from Central Shanghai by metro there is a unique village surrounded by water... A little Venice I can call it!!! When in Shanghai it's a must!!! It is definitely worth 4-5 hours from your time!! Tip: Go by foot and return to Metro Station by Boat! 40 Yuan per person one way.

A good chill-out place to go in Shanghai area. Tourists can get to there by subway directly which is very convenient. Ancient buildings beside the river make people feel like walking in the past. Many restaurants and street foods are available, and tourists can even pay to get on a boat for river sightseeing.

Beautiful little water town with lots of history. Expect to do a lot of walking as the streets are a bit of a maze and lots of little stalls to stop at. Great for lots of local foods at a relatively low price (given it is a tourist location). There are paid attractions but the town itself is free to enter. I particularly enjoyed the soy sauce market/shop which sold many local marinated/pickled goods. Getting to zhujiajiao from shanghai city was relatively simple, albeit a significantly long journey. We too the mtro line 2 from nanjing road to hongqiao airport station, then switched to line 17 to zhujiajiao station. Metro fare was ¥8 one way for an adult. Be reminded that bags need to go through scanning for metros, so leave sharp objects at home. Going into the town, there is the option to hail a ride, rent a bike, or buy a boat ticket. The little boat is 20 min long, ¥40 per person and will take you directly to the middle of the water town, so while pricey, i thought it was worth it. You can send a postcard to yourself at the post office here (they offer international postage), and also visit some temples dating back to the ming/qing dynasty. The night view is spectacular along the river, but the streets will be pitch dark (little to no street lights). Store owners are very friendly and will happily guide you to the metro station if asked. A bit of a walk back to the station (maybe 15 min at a brisk walk) but not too bad. This was one of my favourite tourist spots during my stay in shanghai, so if you like old style buildings/environments, i highly recommend taking the journey here.

You will find lots of shops, tea houses, temples, bridges, gondolas and people, lots of people. Very enjoyable short trip , a perfect place for photos, street food, souvenirs and a glimpse of what life was like in ancient China.

Go at dawn when the tourist shops have closed and the lights have all dimmed, it is a nice experience to just kind of walk around the water town. Very peaceful and picturesque.

DISAPPOINTING AS ITS MOSTLY A TOURIST TRAP The ride out to the "ancient town" on the Shanghai Metro (Line 17) is interesting and cheap (use your Metro pass). The station is a 1.3 km from the town but it's a nice walk on a well signposted road. We went on a cool overcast day but I imagine it wouldn't be very comfortable on a hot, humid day! As you walk to the town from the train station you will pass by some interesting villages which, I think, are far more interesting than the town itself. Lots of gorgeous old stone bridges and simple village environments. Very few people will speak English, so if you can't speak Mandarin you will be pretty much on your own until you get into town. When you get there, expect lots of tourist shops and - believe it or not - a Starbucks Coffee outlet!! You can take a local boat ride while there but you can see just as much by walking along the canal and over the numerous bridges.

Also it has it's own Starbucks if you need a caffeine fix. It was very crowded when we were there. I was too tired but there is some great architecture to shoot. I have a few pictures on my Nikon but it is easier to share the pictures I took with my phone. The people are friendly and didn't notice any shady trouble makers at all so the police are doing a good job. Go have a good time.

Most of the streets are narrow and you can see elements of beautiful traditional Chinese streets foods , habits lifestyle in this ancient town with the old time architecture. you also can find many things to buy that are not that easy to find elsewhere in Shanghai, like traditional Chinese hats, clothes, paintings, jewels and more. We had our lunch at the restaurants along the river, as the food there is with their own recipe and cooking styles it may differs with many other Chinese cuisine, anyway it’s still a great experience in general.

I don't recommend going during CNY, though. It was uncomfortably busy with thousands of visitors. If you go, allow for extra time, and consider taking little breaks along the wall to escape from the crowds. Grab a tea along the river to regain some peace of mind.

Most of the streets are narrow and you can see elements of beautiful traditional Chinese architecture. Just remember that you might need to negotiate the price a little bit, especially if you are a Westerner. The boat-rides around the canals are fantastic and relatively cheap. There are many nice spots to take photos around. The only negative might be the restaurants along the river, as the food there is mediocre and a bit overpriced. A great experience in general.

We bought tickets for the attractions and the boats but we didn't really need to. The place is very walkable and some of the sights were a little repetitive.

Zhujiajiao es el “pueblo de agua” más famoso de Shanghái, un antiguo asentamiento con más de 1.700 años de historia atravesado por canales, puentes de piedra y estrechas callejuelas llenas de casas tradicionales (y de turistas chinos). Conocido como la “Venecia de Shanghái”, ofrece un ambiente tranquilo (si eres capaz de abstraerte del gentío) donde se puede pasear por el puente Fangsheng, probar especialidades locales (sí, aquí comí saltamontes por primera vez, y no están mal) y explorar templos, mercados y patios históricos. Es una escapada perfecta para descubrir la vida tradicional del delta del Yangtsé sin alejarse de la gran ciudad.

從地鐵朱家角站出來後，步行約1.3公里即可抵達古鎮的地標放生橋。這座橋建於明朝嘉靖年間（16世紀），是上海地區現存最大的五孔石橋，橋面寬闊，造型典雅，橫跨漕港河兩岸。站在橋上，白牆黑瓦的民居依水而建，倒映在清澈的河面上，構成一幅典型的江南水鄉畫卷。 白天時，遊人穿梭、船隻緩行，氣氛悠閒；黃昏時分，夕陽灑在水面，古橋與民居映成金光；夜晚燈火亮起，又呈現出溫柔夢幻的景致。 古鎮內店家林立，販售粽子、滷肉、手工藝品與伴手禮，但整體生意似乎不太熱絡。而且，仍有不少人隨地抽煙，非常影響漫步古鎮的體驗。 河水則保持得清澈，水草搖曳，小魚悠遊其間，讓整個水鄉多了幾分生機。若想更貼近水面，可乘坐搖櫓船沿河遊覽，包船約200至300人民幣，能從另一個角度欣賞古橋與民居的倒影。 在朱家角內，除了古橋與街巷外，還有兩處極具特色的園林值得探訪。 一是課植園，始建於清朝，是當地富商的私家花園，以民國初期的水泥建築與西式結構見長。園中佈局開闊，融合中西風格，雖不如蘇州園林精緻細膩，但獨具歷史意義，是了解近代園林轉型的好去處。 另一處則是和心園，被譽為朱家角最值得細細品味的園林。園內假山、曲橋、臨水亭台錯落有致，綠意盎然。尤其園中的臨水書齋與水榭，最能體現江南園林的靜謐與文人氣息。坐在窗邊，望著外頭水巷流淌，令人心境平和。 整體而言，朱家角是一處兼具歷史、人文與自然之美的江南古鎮。 雖然商業化氣息稍重、遊客眾多，但古橋、水鄉與園林仍展現出江南的柔情與古韻，是非常值得安排半日或一日漫遊的景點。

Visitar Zhujiajiao Ancient Town fue una de esas experiencias que se sienten como viajar en el tiempo sin dejar de estar cerca del caos moderno de Shanghai. Este lugar es una joya histórica que combina canales, puentes antiguos, casitas tradicionales y una vibra tranquila que simplemente te envuelve desde el primer paso. Todo parece sacado de una película: el reflejo del agua, los barquitos avanzando lento, y las calles angostas llenas de pequeños negocios locales que mantienen viva la esencia de la zona. Caminar por Zhujiajiao es una experiencia sensorial completa. Entre aromas de comida recién preparada, tiendas de artesanías auténticas y rincones perfectos para fotografías, es imposible no detenerse a contemplar cada detalle. Los snacks locales son toda una aventura por sí solos; algunos dulces, otros salados, otros que todavía no sé si eran postre o algo más, pero todos forman parte del encanto. Las fachadas antiguas, las linternas colgadas y los puentes de piedra crean un ambiente tan especial que es fácil perder la noción del tiempo. Uno de los mejores momentos del recorrido fue el paseo en barca por los canales. Desde el agua, la perspectiva cambia completamente: se ve la arquitectura en su máximo esplendor, la vida cotidiana de los habitantes, y se siente una calma que contrasta de forma perfecta con el dinamismo de Shanghai. Es un espacio que invita a respirar, a bajar el ritmo y simplemente disfrutar. Después de varios días recorriendo ciudades llenas de luces, rascacielos y miles de personas, Zhujiajiao se siente como un descanso necesario. Es ideal para caminar sin prisa, tomar fotos increíbles, probar sabores distintos y vivir un pedacito de la China más tradicional. Sin duda, uno de los lugares más memorables del viaje y un sitio que recomendaría a cualquier persona que quiera conectar con la parte histórica, tranquila y auténtica del país. Un destino hermoso, relajante y lleno de personalidad. Totalmente imprescindible.

朱家角行記——（駢文體敘事） 江南之勝，在水在橋；水鄉之美，因流因居。東南有鎮，名曰 朱家角古鎮，襟吳越而帶滬瀆，枕清流而接煙市。其地也，河汊縱橫，如經如緯；人家對峙，若畫若詩。 是日也，晨光初動，薄霧未收。余易古服，廣袖長衫，步履從容，意在追風雅於前代，寄形骸於水鄉。石板微濕，履聲清越；市聲未作，水韻先聞。白牆映波，黛瓦含煙，遠近相參，虛實互見。 乃登木舟。舟不假帆，行惟憑櫓；櫓動而波生，波平而影定。舟子默然，臂力為歌；水行不疾，時光自遲。舟移橋下，拱石橫空；影入水心，寒光可鑑。或單孔如門，或重孔若虹；石理斑駁，苔痕蒼然。橋上人來人往，橋下水去水還；人事有更，江流無盡。 兩岸人家，臨流而居；窗前修竹，門外繫舟。或老翁倚檐，目送雲水；或稚子逐影，笑落波心。動靜相生，市隱相成，真所謂「居市而不喧，近俗而能遠」者也。 逮乎日暮，景物為變。夕陽西下，金光瀉水；一河皆赤，萬瓦同暉。須臾之間，燈火競起；紅燈映水，明滅相涵。橋影沉沉，舟影緩緩；如星河倒垂，若夢境初開。行於其間，不知身在今夕，抑或遊於往歲。 夜色既深，喧囂漸息。水聲仍在，橋影如常。余解舟登岸，回首長河，但見流光不語，而歲月自明。因歎曰： 水以柔而載史， 橋以靜而通時； 朝代遞嬗， 而江南之韻，千載同歸。 遂書之，以為朱家角一日之記。

上海的朱家角古鎮是一個讓人仿佛置身於歷史畫卷中的地方。這裡被譽為“上海的威尼斯”，充滿了典型的江南水鄉風情。古鎮距離市區約一小時的車程，可以打車前來、也可以乘坐地鐵。 朱家角的美食文化極具特色，是每個來訪者不容錯過的亮點。特別推薦這裡的燒餅大師、阿婆粽、扎肉、海棠糕。燒餅大師的燒餅可以吃梅乾菜燒餅，真的非常美味；也推薦小林阿婆粽的肉粽、扎肉，非常扎實有料！另外角里朱阿婆的海棠糕也是這裡知名的甜點小吃！另外，這裡有很多茶樓，可以在上面品茶，享受古代客官的一天！ 走在古鎮的小巷中，隨處可見的明清古建築讓人目不暇接。比較著名的景點包括課植園和放生橋。課植園曾是明代大儒朱晦庵的私家園林，如今成為了展示江南園林藝術的絕佳場所。而放生橋則是江南古橋的代表，橫跨在蜿蜒的小河上，橋上的雕刻精美，站在橋上可以眺望整個古鎮的風景。此外，還有北大街和東井街這兩條古街，兩側商鋪林立，售賣各種手工藝品和特色小吃。這裡的手工藝品非常精緻，特別是藍印花布和竹編工藝品，值得細細品味和選購。有些景點需要支付票價，但都很便宜沒有什麼壓力。 搭船的部分，游船是以船計價，一次200人民幣，可以和其他人一起併，較為划算。 這裡是忘返的地方，無論是美食、景點還是自然景觀，都充滿了獨特的魅力。這裡既保留了江南水鄉的古樸，又融入了現代的便捷與舒適，是一個適合深入探索、細細品味的好地方。相當推薦來上海一定要來一次！

近年來，水鄉古鎮的旅遊開發越來越同質化，鎮上的零售店、紀念品店、餐飲店都差不多，小商品也多數是自義烏批發來的，缺乏自己的特色。但朱家角古鎮有一個優勢是距離上海比較近，古鎮不遠處設有上海軌道交通17號線的朱家角站，非常方便，工作間隙的週末來去走走還是可以的。 朱家角的主要看點是明代石拱橋——放生橋，課植園，城隍廟，珠溪園等。 這邊緊靠淀山湖風景區，遊玩之餘可以順路過去逛逛，也有水上運動漿板SUP、皮划艇KAYAKING可供娛樂。

岡山の美観地区か大分県の湯布院みたいなやらせの古街観光名所である。ゴミゴミしてて穴だらけで歩きにくい。せめて道路ぐらい整地して欲しい。料理屋も多いが、ガイドがここでは何も食べないでと言うのもうなずける。飯店の生け簀の魚は鯉や鱸であるが、死んで浮かんでるのも多い。あれは食べたらヤバイと思う。あちこちにある土産物屋の清徽园のお土産は箱ばかり大きくて中身は上げ底、隙間だらけ。要注意である。しかし、名物の蒸しパンは美味い。山芋がツナギで入っているようだ。食べてみる価値がある。

Чжуцзяцзяо являются частью Шанхая в часе езды от центра города. Часто Чжуцзяцзяо называют Шанхайская Венеция. Город однозначно старше Шанхая и до сих пор нет точной информации сколько ему лет. В доступных источниках идет речь, что он существовал в эпоху троецарствия. Часть город расположена на суше и не представляет никакого интереса для туристов. Туристическим местом по существу является Северная улица, которая состоит из множества древних домов. В настоящее время практически все дома переоборудованы в торговые ряды, кафе и гостиницы. Только в дальнем конце улицы можно увидеть жилые дома местных жителей. Домики маленькие, в окна отдельных можно рассмотреть очень скудный быт местных. В сторону от центральной улицы отходят очень узкие улочки, ширина которых не больше 1,5-2 метров. Местные по таким улицам передвигаются в основном на мотоциклах и мопедах. Водный транспорт используется конечно в основном для туристических прогулок. Все 36 каменных мостов мы не смогли увидеть, в основном они однотипные. Выделяется на фоне мелких мостов самый крупный пятиарочный каменный мост мост Фаншэн. Поскольку сад Юйюань в Шанхае был закрыт на реконструкцию (октябрь 20169 года), здесь нам удалось посмотреть сад местного чиновника, масштабы которого конечно не сравнимы с первым. Но общее впечатление о структуре и традиционных элементах сада получить можно (вход -20 юаней с человека). Приятно прогуляться в относительной тишине и прохладе под тенью деревьев. Так же можно увидеть убранство жилых комнат, старинную мебель. Есть на Северной улице, на берегу озера Дяньшаньху, местный буддийский храм (вход 10 юаней с человека). При посещении храма мы попали на церемонию прощания с усопшим. Храм хоть и построен по всем канонам, но он провинциальный и не такой помпезный, поэтому по нему бродить было интереснее, чем в крупных и знаменитых. Кругом было много монахов в традиционных одеждах. У данного храма видимо позволяет финансирование кормить малоимущих. Нам тоже предлагали пообедать в храме, но мы вежливо отказались. Место древнее, но весь шарм старины утрачен торговыми рядами для туристов.
